instructions: In a large skillet over medium heat, saute the onion in the olive oil for 3 to 5 minutes, until it begins to brown. Push the onion to one side and add the ground beef; brown for 5 to 7 minutes, breaking it up. When the beef is almost cooked, add the paprika, lemon juice, parsley, pine nuts, salt, and pepper, and cook until done. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Preheat the oven to 375°F and line baking sheets with parchment paper.
On a lightly floured surface, roll the pastry to a 12-by-12-inch square and cut into nine 4-inch squares. Cover and refrigerate while cutting the rest.
Spoon about 2 tablespoons of filling near one corner of each square, fold diagonally into a triangle, and crimp the edges closed with a fork. Place on the baking sheet.
Brush each pastry with the beaten egg and sprinkle with sesame seeds. Refrigerate, uncovered, for 10 minutes.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes, rotating the pans halfway if baking two at once, until puffed and golden brown.
Cool for a few minutes before serving.
notes: Beef-filled borekas (pastelicos) made with store-bought puff pastry. Meat recipe. Source: All Ways Delicious, adapted from The Essential Jewish Baking Cookbook by Beth A. Lee.

tips.text: Puff pastry puffs best when cold going into a hot oven. If the kitchen is warm, chill the cut squares before filling, and don't skip the 10-minute fridge rest before baking.
tips.title: Keep the pastry cold
